title: JOLTS Job Openings (Sep 2026)
source: EST: three bls.gov views fetched direct 2026-09-05 agree — bls.gov/schedule/news_release/jolts.htm reads verbatim 'September 2026 | Nov. 03, 2026 | 10:00 AM', and both bls.gov/schedule/2026/11_sched_list.htm (list view) and 11_sched.htm (month grid) place 'Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey, September 2026' in the Nov 3 10:00 AM slot, with no contradicting view found. Filed estimate DESPITE three agreeing primaries on one count only: this lane does not self-confirm an adjacency it discovered in-sweep — the promotion belongs to this event's own initial-research session, exactly as jolts-2026-12-01 was promoted by its own lane on 2026-09-05 after the chicago-pmi-2026-11-30 sweep filed it. The confirming re-read is the same jolts.htm schedule page
notes: CLOSES AN OPEN ITEM THE SERIES BANKED RATHER THAN GUESSED. The jolts-2026-09-29 pulse of 2026-08-30 identified this exact release as missing from the calendar and deliberately did NOT file it: 'no source-published date was found — BLS's November schedule is not posted and every result was an extrapolation. Proposing a guessed date would manufacture the very thing the EST:/NEWS: prefixes exist to prevent; recorded as an open item for the next pulse instead.' The schedule is posted now, so the item is filed on a primary rather than an extrapolation. THREE THINGS MAKE THIS INSTANCE UNUSUAL. (1) It lands on MIDTERM ELECTION DAY — midterm-elections-2026-11-03 (high impact) — so a medium-impact 10:00 ET slack read publishes into a session whose tape is about something else entirely; expect no attributable footprint. (2) It is the first labor read after fomc-2026-10-28 (the no-SEP meeting) and the last JOLTS before jolts-2026-12-01 and the fomc-2026-12-09 SEP/dot-plot meeting. (3) It is the release MOST exposed to a 2026-10-01 funding lapse: its reference month is September and it publishes ~33 days after government-funding-deadline-2026-09-30 (estimate). The 2025 precedent, read off the JOLTS schedule page's own scar, is that this is the slot a lapse consumes — that page carries no Sep-2025 row and resumes at 'October 2025 | Dec. 09, 2025', while the BLS API still carries 2025-M09 openings of 7,169k, i.e. the data survived and the standalone release did not. Proposed during the jolts-2026-12-01 initial research (2026-09-05).
